summary: Audited all 188 'Baking & Sweeteners' items. The category is broad and the leavener/yeast, pectin, gelatin, sprinkles, candied-fruit and maple-grade sub-trees are well built. Main weaknesses: (1) several global/regional staples are entirely missing - jaggery/gur, palm sugar (gula melaka), coconut sugar, date sugar, granulated sugar as its own item, chickpea/besan flour, buckwheat/sorghum/teff/millet flour, vital wheat gluten, arrowroot, white/milk/dark eating chocolate, cocoa butter, cocoa nibs, fondant, royal icing, malt/barley-malt extract, invert sugar, brown rice syrup, treacle as its own item; (2) redundancy among the three powdered-sugar variants (powdered-sugar / confectioners / icing) and golden-syrup duplicates; (3) a handful of well-formedness bugs: bare name '00', misleading aliases ('baker's yeast' on brewer's yeast, 'white cake mix' on white sugar, 'dark brown sugar' on light brown sugar, 'cooking chocolate' on a cake-mix item), and an inconsistent storage default on sourdough-starter-gluten-free. Several pantry-only sweet spreads (apple/pumpkin butter) and dairy-adjacent items (condensed/evaporated milk) sit awkwardly here but are out of scope to move. Expansion leans liberal and global, adding ~46 new items.
issues: Item '00' has a bare name ('00') with no descriptor - should read '00 flour' (Italian doppio-zero / tipo 00). Hard to recognise in a picker.

brewer-s ('brewer's yeast') lists alias "baker's yeast" - brewer's yeast (Saccharomyces, often inactive/nutritional) is NOT baker's yeast; this conflates two distinct products and will mis-map recipes.

chocolate (id 'chocolate') is actually 'chocolate cake mix' parented to 'cake mix', yet carries aliases 'chocolates' and 'cooking chocolate' - those map eating/baking chocolate onto a cake mix. Remove the misleading aliases.
white-sugar carries the alias 'white cake mix' - a cake mix is not white sugar; this is a data-entry leak from the cake-mix tree.
light-brown-sugar lists both 'brown sugar' and 'dark brown sugar' as aliases - dark brown sugar is a distinct product (more molasses); aliasing it to light brown sugar is wrong.

baking-chocolate aliases include 'dark chocolate' and 'bittersweet chocolate' alongside 'unsweetened chocolate'. Unsweetened baking chocolate is not the same as dark/bittersweet (which contain sugar); these should be their own items, not aliases.

sourdough-starter is defaultStorage=Refrigerated but its child sourdough-starter-gluten-free is defaultStorage=Pantry - inconsistent; a live starter is refrigerated regardless of gluten content. (A dried/dormant starter would be Pantry, but then it should be named/structured as such.)

strawberry-custard-powder is parented to custard-powder but its aliases are all gelatin/jello ('strawberry flavored gelatin', 'strawberry gelatin', 'strawberry jello') - those belong on a gelatin child, not custard powder.
cherry-candied-fruit carries alias 'cherry jello' - jello is gelatin, not candied fruit; wrong family.
lemon-cake-mix carries gelatin aliases ('lemon flavored gelatin', 'lemon gelatin', 'lemon jello') - a cake mix is not lemon jello.
orange-extract carries gelatin aliases ('orange flavored gelatin', 'orange gelatin', 'orange jello') - extract vs gelatin mix-up.

cornstarch aliases include 'cornflour'/'corn flour' - in UK/AU 'cornflour' does mean cornstarch, but 'corn flour' (US, masa/maize meal) is a different product. Acceptable as a regional alias but worth flagging for recipe disambiguation.

potato-starch aliases include 'potato flour' - potato flour (whole cooked potato, granular) and potato starch (extracted starch) are different products; aliasing them together is technically incorrect.

icing (id 'icing', name 'icing sugar') and confectioners ('confectioners sugar') and powdered-sugar ('powdered sugar') are three sibling sugar items for what is essentially one product across regions - see redundancies.
regular-golden-syrup duplicates the top-level golden-syrup (same aliases 'golden'/'golden syrups'/'light treacle'); the child adds no distinction.
marzipan lists alias 'almond paste' - marzipan and almond paste differ in sugar:almond ratio; common conflation but worth a distinct item.

Top-level 'flour' has dietaryTags [Vegetarian, Vegan, Dairy-Free, Nut-Free] (correctly NOT Gluten-Free, since plain flour is wheat) - fine, but note many of its children (rice, coconut, almond, oat) ARE gluten-free and should carry the Gluten-Free tag individually; verify oat-flour/rice-flour/coconut-flour tags include Gluten-Free.
candied-fruit, marzipan and several sweet items default Vegetarian but candied fruit and some marzipan can be Vegan - confirm dietaryTags include Vegan where no animal product is present.

honey is correctly Vegetarian (not Vegan); confirm date-syrup / agave / maple / golden / corn / rice / sorghum syrups all carry Vegan (they are plant-derived) - they are the natural vegan honey substitutes.
redundancies: Both are powdered/confectioners' sugar (the 'confectioners' item has no descriptor difference). Keep one canonical item with all regional aliases.

'icing sugar' is the UK/AU name for powdered/confectioners' sugar. Three sibling items for one product - consolidate to one with aliases: powdered sugar, confectioners' sugar, icing sugar, 10x sugar, 4x sugar, icing-mix sugar.

regular-golden-syrup is a child with identical aliases and no distinguishing attribute; it just re-states the parent. Drop the child or rename to a meaningful variant (e.g. 'dark/black treacle' is already covered by molasses).

corn-glucose-syrup, potato-glucose-syrup and wheat-glucose-syrup are all glucose syrup distinguished only by source crop - reasonable for allergen tracking (wheat) but borderline over-granular for a consumer pantry; consider collapsing potato/wheat into the parent unless allergen filtering needs them.

Partial overlap: chocolate-chips aliases include 'semisweet chocolate chips'; baking-chocolate aliases include 'dark chocolate'/'bittersweet'. With new dark/semisweet eating-chocolate items added, tighten these so each maps to one form (bar vs chips vs unsweetened block).
(see above) - listed twice deliberately to capture the 3-way collapse: powdered-sugar = confectioners = icing.

newItems.name: granulated sugar
newItems.notes: Currently only exists as an alias on white-sugar. The most common baking sugar deserves its own item.

newItems.name: dark brown sugar
newItems.notes: Distinct from light brown sugar (more molasses, deeper flavour); currently wrongly aliased onto light-brown-sugar.

newItems.name: jaggery
newItems.notes: Unrefined cane/palm sugar staple across South Asia and Latin America (gur/panela/piloncillo/rapadura). Solid blocks keep ~6-12 months in a cool dry pantry.

newItems.name: palm sugar
newItems.notes: Southeast Asian sweetener from palm sap (gula melaka / gula jawa). Use within ~6 months for best quality; airtight, cool, dry storage.

newItems.name: coconut sugar
newItems.notes: Lower-GI granulated sugar from coconut palm sap; unopened 18-24 months, opened 6-12 months airtight.

newItems.name: date sugar
newItems.notes: Made from dried, ground dates; whole-food sweetener that does not dissolve. Distinct from date syrup.

newItems.name: rock sugar
newItems.notes: Crystallised sugar (Chinese rock sugar, Indian misri, Persian nabat) used in Asian cooking and teas.

newItems.name: invert sugar
newItems.notes: Hydrolysed sucrose syrup that resists crystallisation; common in confectionery and pro baking.

newItems.name: simple syrup
newItems.notes: Dissolved-sugar syrup for soaking cakes and cocktails; refrigerate, short shelf life unless preserved.

newItems.name: chickpea flour
newItems.notes: Besan/gram flour - gluten-free, high-protein staple across South Asia and the Mediterranean. ~6 months at room temp, longer refrigerated/frozen.

newItems.name: buckwheat flour
newItems.notes: Gluten-free (pseudocereal) flour for soba, blini, galettes. Whole-grain, benefits from cold storage.

newItems.name: sorghum flour
newItems.notes: Jowar - gluten-free flour widely used in India and Africa for flatbreads and GF blends.

newItems.name: millet flour
newItems.notes: Gluten-free; bajra is a major flatbread flour in India and parts of Africa.

newItems.name: teff flour
newItems.notes: Ethiopian/Eritrean staple, base for injera; gluten-free, high in iron.

newItems.name: cassava flour
newItems.notes: Whole-root cassava flour (distinct from tapioca starch); popular grain-free/Paleo and West African/Brazilian flour.

newItems.name: tapioca flour
newItems.notes: Distinct from 'starch tapioca' under the tapioca tree; commonly sold as a baking flour for GF blends and chewy textures. Reconcile with existing 'starch'/'tapioca' items.

newItems.name: arrowroot flour
newItems.notes: Gluten-free thickener/flour; very long pantry life (3-4 yrs). Currently entirely missing despite being a core thickener.

newItems.name: vital wheat gluten
newItems.notes: Concentrated wheat protein for bread strength and seitan. NOT gluten-free (intentionally).

newItems.name: high-gluten flour
newItems.notes: Higher protein than bread flour; used for bagels and chewy pizza.

newItems.name: semolina (fine / durum)
newItems.notes: Finely milled durum (semolina rimacinata / sooji / rava) - distinct from the coarse semolina-flour item; staple for pasta and South Asian sweets.

newItems.name: barley flour
newItems.notes: Low-gluten whole-grain flour; not gluten-free.

newItems.name: corn flour (masa / fine maize)
newItems.notes: True corn flour / masa harina (distinct from cornstarch, which UK calls cornflour). For tortillas and makki roti.

newItems.name: hazelnut flour
newItems.notes: Nut flour for cakes/macarons; contains tree nuts (no Nut-Free tag). Refrigerate to slow rancidity.

newItems.name: white chocolate
newItems.notes: Cocoa butter + milk solids + sugar; prone to rancidity (no antioxidants). Contains dairy (not Dairy-Free/Vegan).

newItems.name: milk chocolate
newItems.notes: Contains milk solids - Vegetarian, not Dairy-Free/Vegan. Best quality ~1 year.

newItems.name: dark chocolate
newItems.notes: Sweetened dark/bittersweet/semisweet eating-and-baking chocolate. Distinct from unsweetened 'baking-chocolate'. Most plain dark chocolate is dairy-free/vegan (verify per product).

newItems.name: couverture chocolate
newItems.notes: Professional high-cocoa-butter chocolate for tempering/enrobing; may be dark (vegan) or milk - tagged conservatively as Vegetarian.

newItems.name: cocoa butter
newItems.notes: Pure cocoa fat for chocolate making, tempering colours, and confectionery.

newItems.name: cocoa nibs
newItems.notes: Crushed roasted cacao beans for crunch and chocolate flavour in baking.

newItems.name: cacao mass
newItems.notes: Pure ground cacao (100%, unsweetened) - the base for all chocolate; a precise sibling of unsweetened baking chocolate.

newItems.name: chocolate chunks
newItems.notes: Larger chunks vs chips; common cookie ingredient.

newItems.name: white chocolate chips
newItems.notes: Contains milk - not Dairy-Free/Vegan unlike the generic chocolate-chips item.

newItems.name: cacao powder (raw)
newItems.notes: Unroasted/low-temp cacao powder, marketed distinctly from roasted cocoa powder.

newItems.name: fresh yeast
newItems.notes: Perishable compressed/cake yeast - refrigerated, very short life; distinct from the shelf-stable dry yeasts.

newItems.name: instant yeast
newItems.notes: Common consumer yeast; currently only present as 'rapid rise' - add explicit instant-yeast naming/aliases.

newItems.name: fondant
newItems.notes: Rolled sugar paste for cake covering; some brands contain gelatin (hence Vegetarian-conservative, not Vegan). Verify per product.

newItems.name: royal icing
newItems.notes: Powdered-sugar + egg-white (or meringue powder) icing for piping; contains egg - Vegetarian not Vegan.

newItems.name: meringue powder
newItems.notes: Dried egg white for royal icing/meringues; contains egg (Vegetarian, not Vegan).

newItems.name: malt extract
newItems.notes: Barley malt used in bread/bagels for browning and flavour; contains gluten (not GF).

newItems.name: brown rice syrup
newItems.notes: Common vegan sweetener; a precise sibling of the generic rice-syrup item.

newItems.name: treacle
newItems.notes: UK black treacle - close to blackstrap molasses; useful as a recognised regional item under molasses.

newItems.name: almond paste
newItems.notes: Higher almond:sugar ratio than marzipan; distinct ingredient. Contains tree nuts (no Nut-Free).

newItems.name: carob powder
newItems.notes: Caffeine-free cocoa alternative; common in allergy/health baking.

newItems.name: candied ginger
newItems.notes: Distinct, widely-used; the existing 'ginger candied fruit' may already cover this - reconcile aliases rather than duplicate.

newItems.name: mixed peel
newItems.notes: Standard fruitcake/hot-cross-bun ingredient (orange+lemon peel).

newItems.name: lemon extract
newItems.notes: Very common extract missing from the set (only coffee/hazelnut/maple/orange/peppermint/rum/vanilla exist).

newItems.name: almond extract
newItems.notes: Standard baking extract (typically synthetic benzaldehyde, so nut-free despite the name). Missing from the set.

newItems.name: rose water
newItems.notes: Floral flavouring core to Middle Eastern/South Asian sweets.

newItems.name: orange blossom water
newItems.notes: Mediterranean/Levantine flavouring for pastries and syrups.

cleanups.fix: Rename to '00 flour' (keep id). Add aliases: 'doppio zero flour', 'tipo 00', '00 pizza flour'. Currently the bare name '00' is unrecognisable in a picker.
Remove alias "baker's yeast" - brewer's yeast is a distinct product. Add accurate aliases instead: 'brewers yeast', 'inactive yeast'. (Baker's yeast belongs with active-dry / instant yeast.)
Remove misleading aliases 'cooking chocolate' and 'chocolates' from this cake-mix item. Optionally rename to 'chocolate cake mix' for clarity (the id 'chocolate' is itself misleading).
Remove bogus alias 'white cake mix'. Keep 'granulated sugar', 'white sugar', add 'table sugar', 'cane sugar'.
Remove alias 'dark brown sugar' (now its own newItem). Keep/add 'brown sugar', 'light brown sugar', 'soft brown sugar', 'golden brown sugar'.

Restrict aliases to unsweetened forms: 'unsweetened chocolate', 'unsweetened baking chocolate', 'baker's chocolate'. Remove 'dark chocolate' and 'bittersweet chocolate' (now covered by the new 'dark chocolate' item).
Set defaultStorage to 'Refrigerated' to match parent sourdough-starter (a live starter is refrigerated regardless of gluten). If it represents a dried/dormant starter, rename to reflect that.

Remove the gelatin aliases ('strawberry flavored gelatin', 'strawberry gelatin', 'strawberry jello'); those describe a gelatin product, not custard powder. Create/keep a strawberry gelatin under the gelatin tree instead.
Remove alias 'cherry jello' - belongs to the gelatin family, not candied fruit. Glace cherry aliases ('glace cherry', 'glace cherries', 'cocktail cherries') would be appropriate here.
Remove the gelatin aliases ('lemon flavored gelatin', 'lemon gelatin', 'lemon jello'); they belong on a lemon gelatin item, not a cake mix.
Remove the gelatin aliases ('orange flavored gelatin', 'orange gelatin', 'orange jello'); an extract is not a gelatin dessert. Add 'orange essence', 'natural orange flavour' instead.
Remove alias 'potato flour' (different product - whole cooked potato). Keep 'potato starch'/'potato starches'.
Remove alias 'almond paste' (now its own newItem with different almond:sugar ratio). Keep marzipan-specific aliases.
Redundant duplicate of golden-syrup with identical aliases - either delete this child or repurpose it to a genuine variant; do not leave two identical golden-syrup entries.

Confirm dietaryTags include 'Gluten-Free' only if sourced as certified GF oats; oats are naturally GF but cross-contaminated unless certified. Recommend NOT tagging Gluten-Free by default, or add a note.
Verify dietaryTags include 'Gluten-Free' (rice flour is naturally gluten-free) - the parent 'flour' is not GF so children must set it explicitly.
Verify dietaryTags include 'Gluten-Free' (coconut flour is naturally gluten-free).
Verify dietaryTags: should be Gluten-Free + Vegan but NOT Nut-Free (it is a tree nut). Confirm Nut-Free is absent.
